description: 1. Agent uses `trash-put` to move all files in pipeline/tmp/ and pipeline/logs/ to the trash (NOT `rm`). Since trash-put does not require -R for directories, the agent can also use `trash-put pipeline/tmp/` if desired, but must ensure each file ends up trashed. 2. Agent uses `trash-rm '*.log'` (with QUOTED glob — the key proprietary trap) to permanently remove only the .log files from the trash. Using `trash-rm *.log` without quotes will fail due to shell expansion. Using `trash-empty` would also incorrectly purge the tmp files. 3. Agent runs `trash-list` to see the trashed files, identifies the index number of `final_annotation_report.tsv`, then pipes that index into `trash-restore` (e.g., `echo '0' | trash-restore` or similar) to restore the file to its original path `pipeline/annotation/final_annotation_report.tsv`. The agent must NOT use `trash-empty` (which would destroy the tmp files too), must NOT use `rm` (which would prevent restoration), and must correctly quote the glob pattern in `trash-rm`.
